body.name: reproducible primal--dual certificate at zero drift
body.construction: Normalize \(M=1\) by scale equivariance. At \(\gamma=0\), index the nine schedules by \((c,t)\in\{-1,0,1\}^2\), where all three control outcomes equal \(c\), the focal treatment outcome equals \(t\), and the target is \(t-c\). The primal hull-plus-singletons policy reports \(\{t-c\}\) on the treatment-assignment record. On the control-assignment record with observed value \(c\), it reports \([-1-c,1-c]\) with probability \(7/10\) and each of \(\{-1-c\}\), \(\{-c\}\), and \(\{1-c\}\) with probability \(1/10\). Thus every schedule has treatment-branch coverage one, control-branch coverage \(8/10\), unconditional coverage \(9/10\), and unconditional expected length \((1/2)(7/10)(2)=7/10\). For the dual, write \(P_s(r)\) for the design probability of record \(r\) under schedule \(s=(c,t)\), set \(\tau_s=t-c\), and let \(\lambda_s,\rho_s\ge0\) be schedule multipliers and \(z_r\) free record multipliers, with constraints \(\sum_sP_s(r)\{\lambda_s\mathbf 1(\tau_s\in I)-\rho_s\operatorname{len}(I)\}+z_r\le0\) for every record--interval pair and \(\sum_s\rho_s\le1\), and objective \((9/10)\sum_s\lambda_s+\sum_rz_r\). Set \(\lambda_{(0,t)}=1\) for \(t\in\{-1,0,1\}\), \(\rho_{(0,-1)}=1\), set \(z_r=-1/2\) at the common control record and at each of the three treatment records with \(c=0\), and set all other multipliers to zero. At every inactive record the dual left side is zero. At the common control record it is \((k(I)-\operatorname{len}(I)-1)/2\le0\), where \(k(I)=|I\cap\{-1,0,1\}|\) and every grid interval obeys \(\operatorname{len}(I)\ge k(I)-1\). At the treatment record with \(t=-1\) it is \(\{\mathbf 1(-1\in I)-\operatorname{len}(I)-1\}/2\le0\); at the treatment records with \(t\in\{0,1\}\) it is \(\{\mathbf 1(t\in I)-1\}/2\le0\). The dual objective is \((9/10)3-4/2=7/10\), matching the primal. Rescaling gives \(\mathfrak L^{(3)}_{0.1,0}=0.7M\).
